caseStudy.title: ArchiveNorth
caseStudy.background:
ArchiveNorth is moving a legal document assistant from a 768-dimension embedding model to a 1024-dimension model. PostgreSQL stores historical embeddings, and Azure Managed Redis caches query results. The team needs quick rollback and must avoid ranking vectors from mixed embedding spaces.

Both revisions of the search API can remain active in Container Apps. Operations wants the first cohort to reach the candidate using a 10% ingress split. The legacy revision and legacy cache must keep working until the candidate passes a relevance check.

Index requests are triggered through Service Bus. During the migration a replayed old update must never overwrite a newer document embedding. Cache keys currently lack model version, and the deployment team wants to measure changes in the p95 vector dependency duration.

exhibits.title: Vector migration plan (SQL excerpt)
exhibits.code:
legacy_embeddings.embedding  vector(768)
candidate_embeddings.embedding  vector(1024)
Distance function: cosine

exhibits.title: Canary measurements
exhibits.code:
stable: p95 request latency 180 ms
candidate: p95 request latency 310 ms
Both revisions: HTTP success rate 99.8%

Write and query versioned embeddings with a query vector from the matching model

questions.prompt: The metro initializer needs 54 seconds. Using a simplified startup budget of periodSeconds × failureThreshold, which threshold is the smallest that provides at least one full additional probe period beyond initialization?

questions.prompt: The metro sender retried within the broker duplicate detection window. Which message property must stay unchanged on an unpartitioned queue?
questions.answer: message_id
questions.explanation: Duplicate detection uses the application-assigned MessageId. Sequence numbers and delivery counts are set by the broker.
options: message_id
locked_until_utc
delivery_count
sequence_number

questions.prompt: The metro Event Grid function receives document version 7 followed by version 6. What should the durable update predicate enforce?
questions.answer: Only apply an event whose version is strictly newer than the stored document version
questions.explanation: Idempotency protects duplicates, while monotonic version checks protect against distinct events arriving out of order.
options: Compare only whether the event IDs differ
Use the delivery retry count to choose the newest document
Always overwrite with the most recently delivered event
Only apply an event whose version is strictly newer than the stored document version

questions.prompt: The metro process is running but should receive traffic only after /healthz/ready succeeds. Which probe should own that endpoint?
questions.answer: readinessProbe
questions.explanation: Readiness is evaluated after startup and controls whether Pods are available for Service traffic.
options: livenessProbe
readinessProbe
startupProbe only
a service selector
